title: sliding-margin-autoscaler-and-util-drift-tracer
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Dedicated capacity pools occasionally oscillate between overprovision and reactive scale-down because short-term utilization spikes bias margin calculators. This leads to transient SLA misses and unnecessary cost. This PR introduces the Sliding Margin Autoscaler (SMA) and a lightweight Utilization Drift Tracer (UDT) to stabilize decisions and provide precise telemetry for ops.

What this changes: Implements an autoscaler policy that computes a sliding-window margin target per pool using a tunable lookback and weighted decay. SMA separates short-term spike handling (soft burst allowance) from persistent demand (reserve commits) by maintaining two sub-budgets: transient_margin and committed_margin. The algorithm rate-limits scale actions and applies an asymmetrical hysteresis to avoid oscillation when utilization drifts around decision boundaries.

Key components:
- controller/autoscaler/sma_controller.go: new controller implementing sliding-window margin logic, delta-based drift detection, and a rate-limited actuation queue.
- controller/autoscaler/metrics_exporter.go: UDT implementation that records per-pool utilization deltas, drift-score, and decision rationales for each scale event.
- pkg/policy/margin_policy.go: policy abstraction supporting transient_margin and committed_margin, with conversion to capacity commands understood by the provisioner.
- helm/templates/autoscaler-config.yaml: feature flag and config knobs for rollout (window_ms, decay_factor, drift_threshold, burst_floor).
- docs/ops/sliding_margin_autoscaler.md: operational runbook and recommended tuning for Dedicated fleets.

Design notes: SMA calculates a weighted moving average of utilization percentiles (P50/P90) over a sliding window, then computes the delta between the short and long windows to produce a drift_score. If drift_score exceeds drift_threshold, the controller favors committed_margin growth; otherwise it prefers transient_margin adjustments. Burst allowances are budgeted per-pool and reconciled against warm-pool capacity to avoid unbounded cost. All scale proposals are stamped with a decision_reason (e.g., "p90-drift", "sustained-growth", "safety-fallback") and exported via UDT for traceability.

Compatibility and rollout: Backwards-compatible with existing autoscaler interfaces. Feature is gated by helm feature flag autoscaler.sma.enabled=false by default. Rollout plan: canary on 5% of Dedicated pools for 48h, compare latency SLOs, cost delta, and scale churn against control group.

Testing & CI: Unit tests for policy math, property tests for hysteresis boundaries, e2e integration tests with synthetic traffic ramp, and a harnessed soak test for 72h under realistic burst patterns. CI shows all checks passing; e2e tests were run with mocked provisioner.

Operational telemetry added:
- redwood.autoscaler.sma.drift_score{pool}
- redwood.autoscaler.sma.transient_margin{pool}
- redwood.autoscaler.sma.committed_margin{pool}
- redwood.autoscaler.sma.decision_reason{pool}
- redwood.autoscaler.sma.scale_actions{result}

Checklist:
- [x] Algorithm implemented and covered by unit tests
- [x] Telemetry exported and documented
- [x] Helm flags and defaults added
- [x] Docs runbook written
- [x] Canary rollout plan included

Related work: ENG-2041 (warm-pool accounting) and ENG-1987 (scale event tracing). Linear: ENG-2157 tracks implementation; ENG-2203 tracks rollout and postmortem.

Merge outcome: merged via squash and merge after addressing a telemetry tagging nit and adding a defensive nil-check in the actuation queue.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Please add an explicit safety cap on transient_margin so we don't accidentally consume warm-pool capacity. Also suggest exposing drift_threshold as a percent of p90 rather than absolute CPU util.
Maya Chen (author): Added transient_margin cap and converted threshold to relative p90 percent. See commit 'fix: defensive nil-check in actuation queue (review feedback)'.
Sofia Patel: Can we surface the decision_reason in the Console UI traces? It will help SREs understand why scale ops fired during incidents.
Maya Chen: Filed ENG-2203 to track Console integration; added decision_reason to UDT telemetry so Console team can consume it.
Arjun Rao: Nit: use context.WithTimeout in the controller reconcile loop to avoid stuck goroutines during heavy provisioner latency.
Maya Chen: Applied change and added test asserting reconcile respects context cancellation.
